concepts.description: Building an uncertainty range by starting from an impossibly wide bound and narrowing toward plausibility avoids the anchoring trap of starting from a single point-estimate and padding it.
concepts.title: Absurdity Test for Range Estimation

concepts.description: Reviewing a document in a fixed pass order — technical accuracy, then completeness, then structure, then clarity — so effort on prose polish never gets wasted on content that turns out to be wrong.
concepts.title: Accuracy-First Review Ordering

concepts.description: A verification methodology that avoids leading or yes/no questions, forcing sources or test systems to independently produce data to prevent passive confirmation bias.
concepts.title: Active Recall Verification

concepts.description: Having independent parties each search for and present the strongest evidence for opposing conclusions, rather than one party assembling a case for a single predetermined answer, so a judge sees the strongest evidence on both sides instead of only the side someone chose to look for.
concepts.title: Adversarial Evidence Elicitation

concepts.description: Actively searching for a better or alternative explanation before accepting the first explanation offered for an observed pattern.
concepts.title: Alternative Hypothesis Consideration

concepts.description: Verifying not just individual facts but whether they collectively support the document's overarching argument and conclusions.
concepts.title: Argument-Level Verification

concepts.description: Checking an assumed equivalence or invariant against live data with an assertion or log before committing to a change or claim that depends on it.
concepts.title: Assumption Verification Via Runtime Instrumentation

concepts.description: In peer review, the author owns approach choices among equally valid options; the reviewer verifies comprehension and material defects, not personal taste.
concepts.title: Author Deference in Technical Review

concepts.description: Methods and mental strategies for individuals to effectively verify their own writing and technical claims.
concepts.title: Author Self-Verification

concepts.description: Running mechanical verifiers (tests, linters, static analysis) before a human reviewer sees a change so review effort focuses on substance, not formatting.
concepts.title: Automated Checks Before Human Review

concepts.description: The dangerous assumption that automated system outputs and software logs are inherently correct without independent audit trails.
concepts.title: Automation Bias in Verification

concepts.description: Holding action on a high-stakes verdict until the designated confirmatory check completes, rather than treating a preliminary expert judgment as final.
concepts.title: Awaiting Confirmatory Evidence

concepts.description: Misjudging a positive test result's reliability by ignoring how rare the condition being tested for actually is in the population.
concepts.title: Base Rate Fallacy

concepts.description: When the probability you actually need is hard to estimate directly, estimate the easier reverse conditional probability instead and use Bayes' theorem to invert it into the answer you need.
concepts.title: Bayesian Inversion Technique

concepts.description: Validating performance assertions by cross-checking measurement tool output against independent telemetry and guarding against harness artifacts.
concepts.title: Benchmark Claim Verification

concepts.description: Selecting a subgroup on a combination of two otherwise-unrelated traits can create an artificial negative correlation between those traits within the selected subgroup alone.
concepts.title: Berkson's Paradox

concepts.description: Grouping continuous data into bins can manufacture or hide an apparent trend, through uneven bin widths or through averaging away the underlying spread.
concepts.title: Binning-Induced Distortion

concepts.description: Verifying a claim produced by an opaque method (statistical model, algorithm, or specialized apparatus) by checking its input data and output plausibility rather than its internal workings.
concepts.title: Black-Box Claim Verification

concepts.description: Concealing which condition a subject or evaluator is in prevents both parties' expectations from contaminating a test's result, and this can be done cheaply without specialist resources.
concepts.title: Blinding to Prevent Bias

concepts.description: Whether a stated confidence level (a 90% range, a 70% chance) actually matches the real hit rate is a measurable, trainable skill, and most untrained people are systematically overconfident.
concepts.title: Calibrated Probability Assessment

concepts.description: Estimating the size of a hidden or uncountable population by taking two independent samples and measuring how much they overlap — the smaller the overlap, the larger the true population.
concepts.title: Capture-Recapture Estimation

concepts.description: Practices that mimic the outward form of science — titles, case studies, confident authorities — without the doubt, testing, and falsification that make evidence reviewable.
concepts.title: Cargo Cult Science

concepts.description: Matching a claim's wording, mood, and framing to whether the underlying evidence is observational (associational) or interventional (causal).
concepts.title: Causal Language Calibration

concepts.description: The summary and body of a proposed change should document what changed and why, because they become the searchable audit trail future reviewers rely on.
concepts.title: Change Description as Verification Record

concepts.description: A baseline captured directly from a system's actual current output is valid evidence for detecting future drift, even though it is not evidence the behavior is correct.
concepts.title: Characterization Baseline as a Verification Oracle

concepts.description: Before attributing an error to bad faith, checking whether the reviewer is mistaken or whether an honest mistake fully explains it.
concepts.title: Charitable Interpretation in Review

concepts.description: Borrowing a visualization form's implied structure or rigor (a periodic table, subway map, or Venn diagram) for data that doesn't actually share that structure.
concepts.title: Chart Form Mismatch

concepts.description: Checking whether a chart's scale, axis range, or aggregation choice (rather than the underlying data) is what produces its apparent trend.
concepts.title: Chart Framing Verification

concepts.description: The selective presentation of data or sources that support a specific conclusion while ignoring conflicting evidence.
concepts.title: Cherry-Picking

concepts.description: What must be cited — not just facts, but any borrowed idea, wording, data point, or distinctive structure — so a reader can independently trace and check the material.
concepts.title: Citation Completeness Check

concepts.description: Matching the scope and confidence of technical assertions directly to the empirical reach of the underlying methodology.
concepts.title: Claim Scope Calibration

concepts.description: Matching the kind of evidence required to a claim's type — factual, definitional, causal, evaluative, or practical — since each type needs a different kind of support.
concepts.title: Claim Type Taxonomy

concepts.description: The practice of prioritizing checkable claims based on external dependencies, risk level, and ease of verification to optimize the review schedule.
concepts.title: Claim Verification Triage

concepts.description: Independent review primarily verifies that a change is understandable and maintainable by others, not that it matches the reviewer's preferred approach.
concepts.title: Code Review Comprehension Priority

concepts.description: The reasoning error of treating the probability of evidence given a hypothesis as if it were the probability of the hypothesis given the evidence.
concepts.title: Conditional Probability Inversion

concepts.description: People confidently fabricate plausible-sounding explanations for their own behavior and motives without realizing it, so direct questions about "why" are unreliable evidence — specific-recall questions about a recent concrete instance are more trustworthy.
concepts.title: Confabulation in Testimony

concepts.description: A frequentist confidence interval is a statement about the interval-construction procedure, not the probability that a fixed parameter lies inside one observed interval.
concepts.title: Confidence Interval Interpretation

concepts.description: The tendency to under-scrutinize claims that match a reviewer's existing beliefs and over-scrutinize claims that don't.
concepts.title: Confirmation Bias in Verification

concepts.description: A third, often unmeasured factor that independently causes both halves of an observed association, making the two look causally linked when they aren't.
concepts.title: Confounding Variables

concepts.description: Abstract properties that can't be measured directly (culture, quality, satisfaction) need multiple converging indicators, not one proxy metric, before a claim about them can be trusted.
concepts.title: Construct Validity Through Multi-Item Measurement

concepts.description: A safeguard designed to limit the blast radius of an undetected defect is a different thing from a check designed to detect the defect, and treating a clean pass of the former as evidence of correctness lets verification quietly erode.
concepts.title: Containment Mechanisms Are Not Verification

concepts.description: Shifting authenticity verification upstream by cryptographically signing an image, video, or article at the moment of capture or publication, rather than each downstream checker re-authenticating it after the fact.
concepts.title: Content Provenance Authentication

concepts.description: Designing a process so it emits verifiable evidence of its own operation as a byproduct of doing the work, rather than reconstructing evidence after the fact through manual sampling.
concepts.title: Continuous Audit Evidence Generation

concepts.description: Treating verification as an ongoing background process rather than a one-time check, since silent corruption can occur after a fact was first confirmed true.
concepts.title: Continuous Integrity Auditing

concepts.description: Bots, fake accounts, and sockpuppets can manufacture the appearance of independent corroboration or popular consensus where none exists.
concepts.title: Coordinated Inauthentic Amplification

concepts.description: Refuting a false claim takes far more effort than producing it, and even a fully successful, widely-publicized correction rarely reaches everyone who saw the original — implications for prioritizing verification effort.
concepts.title: Correction Effort Asymmetry

concepts.description: What a correlation coefficient does and does not establish — including sensitivity to outliers, blindness to nonlinear relationships, and silence on practical magnitude.
concepts.title: Correlation Coefficient Limitations

concepts.description: Why an observed association between two variables does not by itself establish which one causes the other, or that either causes anything at all.
concepts.title: Correlation vs. Causation

concepts.description: A single case that satisfies a claim's premise but not its conclusion is often a cheaper and more decisive check than a full technical rebuttal.
concepts.title: Counterexample Refutation

concepts.description: Verifying a claim by checking whether separate sections or documents describing the same underlying reality are internally consistent with each other, not just individually accurate.
concepts.title: Cross-Statement Consistency Check

concepts.description: Robert Merton's four norms for a trustworthy knowledge-producing community — shared data, source-blind evaluation, vigilance against conflicts of interest, and organized dissent — usable as a checklist for whether any group's truth-seeking process, not only a scientific one, deserves trust.
concepts.title: CUDOS Scientific Norms

concepts.description: A model built from many candidate predictor variables can fit a training dataset by chance alone, which requires exponentially more data to rule out as the variable count grows.
concepts.title: Curse of Dimensionality Overfitting Risk

concepts.description: When a study's observation window ends before an outcome has occurred for some subjects, dropping or misclassifying those still-ongoing cases and skewing the result.
concepts.title: Data Censoring

concepts.description: Three specific ways an investigator can distort a timeline of events while assembling evidence — comparing fragments against hindsight standards, cherry-picking quotes to fit a preset label, and bundling weak sequential cues as if they arrived together.
concepts.title: Decontextualization Traps in Investigation

concepts.description: People believe a new statement automatically on first encountering it and only sometimes vet it afterward, rather than withholding belief until it's checked — which is the underlying reason unverified claims spread by default rather than by exception.
concepts.title: Default Belief Formation

concepts.description: A field initialized to a default value and updated only when a separate confirming feed arrives is indistinguishable from a genuine negative when that feed silently fails, so its completeness must be verified independently of the field's own stored value.
concepts.title: Default-Negative Values Masking Missing Signal

concepts.description: The process of identifying and isolating testable assertions within a document to prepare them for verification.
concepts.title: Defining Checkable Claims

concepts.description: A shrinking or slower-growing share of a total can mask a rising absolute number, if the denominator itself is changing.
concepts.title: Denominator Manipulation

concepts.description: Using code review to verify implementation against settled design, not to reopen architecture or API decisions that belong in earlier review forums.
concepts.title: Design Decisions Outside Code Review

concepts.description: The first independent reviewer adds the most verification value; each additional reviewer adds less while coordination cost grows quickly.
concepts.title: Diminishing Returns of Extra Reviewers

concepts.description: Independently rescaling two y-axes on the same chart can force two unrelated series to visually appear correlated, and a physically impossible axis range is a strong tell that this happened.
concepts.title: Dual-Axis Manipulation Detection

concepts.description: Tracing every path by which a change's effects can become observable, so verification neither misses silently-affected areas nor wastes effort on unaffected ones.
concepts.title: Effect Propagation Analysis for Verification Scope

concepts.description: Publishers rewarded by clicks rather than by long-term reader trust are structurally incentivized to sacrifice accuracy for emotional pull, producing detectable headline and framing patterns.
concepts.title: Engagement Incentive Distortion

concepts.description: Capturing a durable copy of an online or otherwise perishable source at the moment it's consulted, since links die, pages change, and posts get deleted.
concepts.title: Ephemeral Source Preservation

concepts.description: Explicitly distinguishing raw empirical data, direct logical inferences, and broader speculative interpretations within technical claims.
concepts.title: Epistemic Level Separation

concepts.description: A forced comparison against a fair random device — would you rather bet on your stated range being right, or spin a dial with your stated odds — reveals whether a confidence level is genuinely felt or just a verbal habit.
concepts.title: Equivalent Bet Calibration Test

concepts.description: Classifying a discovered factual error by how much damage it does to a document, from a simple copy error up through fabrication, to prioritize the response.
concepts.title: Error Severity Taxonomy

concepts.description: Techniques for reading and vetting academic papers, preprints, and research studies for factual accuracy and consensus alignment.
concepts.title: Evaluating Scientific Literature

concepts.description: Five properties — accuracy, precision, sufficiency, representativeness, and appropriateness — that evidence must satisfy to actually support the specific claim it's cited for.
concepts.title: Evidence Quality Dimensions

concepts.description: The distinction between how confidently evidence supports a causal link and how large that link's real-world effect actually is.
concepts.title: Evidence Strength vs. Effect Magnitude

concepts.description: Verifying claims by cross-checking them across multiple independent sources to avoid circular sourcing and aggregation errors.
concepts.title: Evidence Triangulation

concepts.description: The practice of evaluating and presenting sources based on the weight of technical consensus rather than providing equal representation to fringe or unverified viewpoints.
concepts.title: Evidence Weighting vs. False Balance

concepts.description: Why randomized manipulation of a variable provides stronger causal evidence than an observed association, and how converging independent manipulations build further confidence.
concepts.title: Experimental vs. Observational Causal Evidence

concepts.description: Heuristics for catching invented facts, sources, or quotes, including the risk that a reviewer under-scrutinizes celebrated authors.
concepts.title: Fabrication Detection

concepts.description: Dismissing relevant reference-class or comparable data as inapplicable by treating the current case as too unique for outside data to bear on it, when the situations actually share the structure that matters.
concepts.title: Fallacy of Close Analogy

concepts.description: Deriving an independent order-of-magnitude estimate from roughly-known factors to test whether a stated figure is even plausible.
concepts.title: Fermi Estimation for Verification

concepts.description: A propaganda strategy that aims not to convince of one specific falsehood but to exhaust critical scrutiny through sheer volume and self-contradiction.
concepts.title: Firehose of Falsehood

concepts.description: Explaining away each new piece of disconfirming evidence individually, one reasonable-seeming step at a time, can walk a conclusion far off course without any single step ever feeling like a red flag.
concepts.title: Garden Path Fallacy

concepts.description: A metric that becomes a target stops being a trustworthy measure, because the people or systems it evaluates adapt to optimize the metric rather than the underlying goal it was meant to track.
concepts.title: Goodhart's Law

concepts.description: Checking whether a measured improvement following an intervention could be an artifact of participants knowing they were being observed or studied, rather than the intervention itself.
concepts.title: Hawthorne Effect Check

concepts.description: Using calibrated qualifying language to represent a claim's actual confidence level instead of asserting it as settled fact.
concepts.title: Hedge Words for Uncertain Claims

concepts.description: Anchoring an ungrounded, hard-to-quantify claim by asking calibrated judges to compare it in relative magnitude against a known, well-measured reference event, even when the reference is only loosely related.
concepts.title: Heterogeneous Benchmarking

concepts.description: Knowing an outcome distorts a reviewer's judgment of how predictable and preventable it was, and of the quality of the decisions that led to it — a specific bias to guard against when evaluating past decisions or incidents.
concepts.title: Hindsight Bias in Review

concepts.description: More experience, more data, or more analytical effort routinely increases a person's confidence in their own judgment without any corresponding increase, or even with a decrease, in actual accuracy.
concepts.title: Illusion of Learning

concepts.description: The tendency for repeated exposure to a claim to increase its perceived credibility, independent of whether the claim is actually accurate.
concepts.title: Illusory Truth Effect

concepts.description: Techniques for confirming a photo or video is genuine, correctly contextualized, and not AI-generated or miscontextualized.
concepts.title: Image Authenticity Verification

concepts.description: The prospect of a highly desirable outcome activates reward-anticipation psychology that suppresses critical scrutiny, distinct from confirmation bias or over-familiarity.
concepts.title: Incentive Bias in Verification

concepts.description: Structuring failure evidence and timeline data in postmortems to ensure independent auditability and root cause verification.
concepts.title: Incident Postmortem Verification

concepts.description: What makes a safety or failure investigation's conclusions evidence-based rather than merely negotiated is rigorous, independent, scientific fact-finding — not consensus among the stakeholders who have a stake in the outcome.
concepts.title: Independent Forensic Investigation as the Basis for Evidence-Based Consensus

concepts.description: Stating an assumed invariant explicitly as a checkable assertion at the point it is established, not merely wherever it is relied upon.
concepts.title: Invariant Assertion Placement

concepts.description: The cognitive tendency of reviewers to skip verifying assertions that align with their own expertise or prior knowledge.
concepts.title: Knowledge Bias in Verification

concepts.description: Quantifying, rather than assuming, how much an LLM-based pairwise judge's verdicts can be trusted by comparing them against a separately computed, non-LLM metric and reporting the actual agreement rate.
concepts.title: Cross-Validating LLM-as-Judge Evaluations Against an Independent Metric

concepts.description: Identifying formulas that look mathematically rigorous while the specific arithmetic operations they use aren't actually justified by anything.
concepts.title: Mathiness Detection

concepts.description: Checking whether a reported average was chosen because it best represents the data, or because it tells a more favorable story.
concepts.title: Mean vs. Median Selection

concepts.description: A precise-sounding number that is technically accurate but omits the comparison needed to actually interpret it.
concepts.title: Meaningless Numerosity

concepts.description: A measurement is a quantitatively expressed reduction of uncertainty from observation, not a demand for certainty — and a figure with no stated error range is a sign it may not be a real measurement at all.
concepts.title: Measurement as Uncertainty Reduction

concepts.description: Three distinct meanings of "causes" that must not be substituted for one another when evaluating a causal claim.
concepts.title: Necessary, Sufficient, and Probabilistic Cause

concepts.description: A quick diagnostic for prose so unclear it can't be pinned down and therefore can't be checked — if negating a sentence doesn't change its meaning, it isn't making a checkable claim.
concepts.title: Negation Test for Vacuous Claims

concepts.description: Several popular epistemic maxims claim a non-conclusive observation tells you nothing, but Bayes' theorem shows any observation that would be conclusive if it went the other way must shift belief even when it doesn't.
concepts.title: Non-Conclusive Evidence Still Shifts Probability

concepts.description: A practice that once departed from the accepted norm becomes the new accepted norm through a long chain of small, individually-defensible steps, each one invisible as a departure because the gap from the immediately preceding step is too small to notice or report.
concepts.title: Normalization of Deviance

concepts.description: Building a deliberately boring simulation with no real effect to check whether an observed pattern could arise without the mechanism being claimed.
concepts.title: Null Model Testing

concepts.description: Cross-checking a quantitative claim against context, common sense, and unit consistency before accepting it as verified.
concepts.title: Numeric Sanity Checking

concepts.description: Testing a claim against the objections, alternatives, and limitations a thoughtful reviewer would predictably raise, and responding to each proportionately, before the document is reviewed.
concepts.title: Objection Anticipation in Argument Construction

concepts.description: When the act of observing something is itself correlated with the state being measured, making a routine or unbiased process feel systematically unlucky.
concepts.title: Observation Selection Effect

concepts.description: The practice of identifying missing evidence, data points, or perspectives that make an otherwise factually accurate document misleading.
concepts.title: Omission Detection

concepts.description: Adding, weighting, or averaging ordinal-scale ranks (star ratings, risk levels, severity tiers) as if they were true numeric quantities is invalid, because the scale has no fixed unit distance between values.
concepts.title: Ordinal Scale Arithmetic Fallacy

concepts.description: The common error of reading a p-value as the probability a hypothesis is true, rather than as the probability of the observed data under the null hypothesis.
concepts.title: P-Value Misinterpretation

concepts.description: Catching statements that are literally true but engineered to create a false impression, or that use vague phrasing specifically to dodge accountability.
concepts.title: Paltering and Weasel-Wording Detection

concepts.description: Running an old and new system side by side against the same input and comparing outputs is a direct way to verify equivalence, but the reference oracle it relies on may be a buggy legacy system rather than a correct one.
concepts.title: Parallel-Run Parity Verification

concepts.description: Running incomplete verification is better than not running a theoretically complete verification plan you never actually execute.
concepts.title: Partial Verification Over Unexecuted Completeness

concepts.description: A percentage change depends entirely on which value is used as the denominator, and the same underlying numbers can support very different percentages depending on that choice.
concepts.title: Percentage Base Ambiguity

concepts.description: "Percent of total change" claims can exceed 100% or go negative when the components being summed have mixed signs, producing numbers that look meaningful but aren't.
concepts.title: Percentage Contribution Fallacy

concepts.description: Six criteria for deciding whether a technically-correct objection is worth raising, distinguishing genuine correction from scoring a irrelevant point.
concepts.title: Pertinence Test for Objections

concepts.description: A checklist for evaluating whether a poll or survey is a credible primary source before a claim relies on it.
concepts.title: Poll Methodology Assessment

concepts.description: Requiring independent review and explicit consent before a change enters shared state, so verification happens while rollback is still cheap.
concepts.title: Pre-Commit Peer Review

concepts.description: A measurement can be highly reproducible yet systematically wrong (precise but inaccurate), or noisy yet correct on average (accurate but imprecise) — and a reviewer should identify which kind of error, if any, a cited figure carries before trusting it.
concepts.title: Precision vs. Accuracy in Measurement

concepts.description: Defining exactly what result will count as confirming or disconfirming a claim before gathering the evidence, so ambiguous results can't be rationalized after the fact.
concepts.title: Precommitted Evaluation Criteria

concepts.description: Verifying that a data-driven predictive model's demonstrated accuracy reflects durable causal structure rather than incidental correlations that will decay or self-undermine over time.
concepts.title: Predictive Model Generalization Check

concepts.description: Reframing a plan review as "imagine it already failed, now explain why" breaks the emotional attachment that makes people scrutinize their own plans only half-heartedly.
concepts.title: Premortem Technique

concepts.description: Transparently showing an unresolved conflict between credible sources rather than forcing a false single answer.
concepts.title: Presenting Genuine Source Disagreement

concepts.description: The distinction between raw original evidence and interpretative summaries, and how to evaluate their credibility in verification.
concepts.title: Primary vs. Secondary Sources

concepts.description: Deliberately injecting real failures into a live production system to generate empirical evidence for resilience claims that are otherwise too complex to verify by inspection or staged testing alone.
concepts.title: Production Fault Injection Verification

concepts.description: Walking a reviewer through the evidence and intermediate steps that led to a conclusion, in the order they were discovered, instead of presenting the conclusion first and the reasoning as backup.
concepts.title: Progressive Reasoning Disclosure

concepts.description: The shaded area or length used to represent a value in a chart must be directly proportional to that value, and violations of this rule are a specific, checkable way charts distort accurate data.
concepts.title: Proportional Ink Principle

concepts.description: Removing a sensitive or protected variable from a model or comparison does not eliminate its influence if other, correlated variables still leak the same signal.
concepts.title: Proxy Variable Leakage

concepts.description: A technical-sounding label that merely redescribes the outcome it's meant to explain, creating an illusion of explanation through circular reasoning.
concepts.title: Pseudo-Explanatory Labels

concepts.description: The systematic tendency for positive/significant results to reach publication while negative results go unpublished, distorting the apparent weight of evidence.
concepts.title: Publication Bias

concepts.description: Evaluating verification thoroughness using qualitative depth tiers rather than misleading quantitative coverage percentages.
concepts.title: Qualitative Coverage Depth

concepts.description: A claim dressed in numbers, statistics, or technical jargon reads as rigorous by default, even when the underlying reasoning doesn't hold up — and reviewers tend to under-challenge it for exactly that reason.
concepts.title: Quantitative Authority Illusion

concepts.description: Methods for confirming a quoted statement is accurate, in context, and correctly attributed before it is published.
concepts.title: Quote Verification Techniques

concepts.description: Accepting a claim's own assumptions and extrapolating them to a self-evidently absurd conclusion to expose a flawed model without needing outside evidence.
concepts.title: Reductio ad Absurdum Refutation

concepts.description: The confusion between a claim's proportional change and its real-world magnitude, which can make a negligible effect sound alarming.
concepts.title: Relative Risk vs. Absolute Risk

concepts.description: The documented tendency for a large share of published research findings to fail when independently reproduced, which bounds how much weight a single study should carry.
concepts.title: Replication Crisis

concepts.description: Practical discipline for publishing a correction responsibly — verifying it thoroughly, admitting fault quickly if wrong, and communicating it clearly.
concepts.title: Responsible Refutation Practice

concepts.description: Review artifacts preserve who approved what, why a change was made, and how decisions were discussed — enabling later independent verification ("code archaeology").
concepts.title: Review as Historical Record

concepts.description: Reviewer thoroughness degrades non-linearly as the size of a single reviewed unit grows, so a reviewable submission should be kept small rather than comprehensive.
concepts.title: Review Batch Size Effect

concepts.description: Structured conventions for unresolved vs. optional comments, batch publishing, and tracking whose turn it is to act — so review threads stay checkable.
concepts.title: Review Comment Resolution Conventions

concepts.description: Different change categories — greenfield, behavior change, bug fix, rollback, large-scale refactor — warrant different verification focus and review strictness.
concepts.title: Review Scope by Change Type

concepts.description: Complex system failures typically arise from multiple factors that are individually necessary and only jointly sufficient, so a single "root cause" is a constructed stopping point for an investigation, not a discovered fact.
concepts.title: Root Cause Fallacy

concepts.description: A random sample of just five observations from any population is already 93.75% likely to bracket that population's true median between its smallest and largest values.
concepts.title: Rule of Five

concepts.description: Checking how a number was actually produced — from a full count, a biased sample, a self-reported measurement, or an indirect model — before trusting its precision.
concepts.title: Sampling and Measurement Bias

concepts.description: When the sampled individuals or cases differ systematically from the population a claim is about, with respect to the exact thing being measured.
concepts.title: Selection Bias

concepts.description: Subjective perception surveys and objectively measured outcomes are different evidence tiers, even when both point the same direction, and shouldn't be cited interchangeably for an effectiveness claim.
concepts.title: Self-Report vs. Objective Outcome Evidence

concepts.description: A claim about an internal computation or effect cannot be checked at all until some channel exists to observe it, so creating that channel is itself part of verification work.
concepts.title: Sensing as a Verification Precondition

concepts.description: Splitting independent review into distinct approval bits — correctness, ownership fit, and standards conformance — so each check can be performed by the right reviewer.
concepts.title: Separated Review Approval Roles

concepts.description: Estimating a total production or population count from the clustering of sequential identifiers observed in a small, non-random sample — a technique that famously out-performed espionage in WWII.
concepts.title: Serial Number Population Estimation

concepts.description: Checking whether a model's high measured performance comes from a spurious artifact in its training data rather than the capability actually being claimed.
concepts.title: Shortcut Learning Verification

concepts.description: A four-step information-literacy process for evaluating claims and tracing them back to their original context.
concepts.title: SIFT Framework

concepts.description: A calculated result can never be reported to more significant digits than its least-precise input actually supports, no matter how many digits the arithmetic produces.
concepts.title: Significant Digit Discipline

concepts.description: An aggregate association between two variables can reverse or disappear once a confounding stratification variable is controlled for.
concepts.title: Simpson's Paradox

concepts.description: Under maximum prior uncertainty about which of two outcomes is more common, examining just one random observation already raises the odds of correctly identifying the majority from 50% to 75%.
concepts.title: Single Sample Majority Rule

concepts.description: When a quantity is measured by counting units (classes, groups, hosts) instead of the members within them, small units are structurally over-represented relative to what most members actually experience.
concepts.title: Size-Biased Sampling

concepts.description: A source's status as primary and reliable is scoped to the specific claim within their direct firsthand knowledge or expertise, not a blanket property of the person or document.
concepts.title: Source Authority Scope

concepts.description: A set of angles for finding genuine problems in a source's argument — beyond correlation-versus-causation — once it has been understood well enough to summarize fairly.
concepts.title: Source Critique Strategies

concepts.description: Checking whether a claim is supported by a specific cited source is a more accurate and more consistent task than judging the claim's truth directly, but only if the cited source was chosen fairly rather than persuasively.
concepts.title: Source-Grounded Evaluation Simplifies Verification

concepts.description: Three questions for triaging a claim's credibility before deeper verification — who is saying it, how would they know, and what are they trying to sell.
concepts.title: Source Motive Checklist

concepts.description: Under time pressure, weighting accounts from parties closest to an event or system and confirming directly with the responsible institution before repeating unverified reports.
concepts.title: Source Proximity Heuristic

concepts.description: A checklist of signals for judging how much a source can be trusted, none individually conclusive, evaluated separately from whether the source is relevant.
concepts.title: Source Reliability Indicators

concepts.description: Recognizing correlations that arise from chance or shared trends rather than any real connection, especially when many series are compared at once.
concepts.title: Spurious Correlation Detection

concepts.description: A claim or document that was accurately verified when written can become false later through ordinary drift, so verification needs an ongoing maintenance owner, not just a one-time author.
concepts.title: Stale Evidence Maintenance

concepts.description: Across decades of tested comparisons, simple statistical models have beaten unaided expert judgment far more often than the reverse, so a claim resting purely on expert intuition should be weighed against that documented track record, not assumed superior by default.
concepts.title: Statistical Model Track Record vs. Expert Judgment

concepts.description: How significance thresholds trade off false-positive (type 1) and false-negative (type 2) errors, and why power depends on specifying what "false" concretely means.
concepts.title: Statistical Type Errors and Power

concepts.description: Searching for evidence only where existing tools or familiarity make looking convenient, rather than where the answer is actually likely to be found.
concepts.title: Streetlight Effect

concepts.description: Drawing conclusions only from the cases that survived some selection process to become observable, while the systematically missing, unobserved cases carry the more important information.
concepts.title: Survivorship Bias

concepts.description: Deliberately injecting a known fault and confirming the check reports failure before trusting that check as a verification oracle.
concepts.title: Test Oracle Self-Validation

concepts.description: Verifying a claim about a machine-learning system's output by scrutinizing the data it was trained on, rather than needing to understand its internal algorithm.
concepts.title: Training Data Provenance Check

concepts.description: A generative model tends to continue and build on a false or nonsensical premise already present in its input rather than questioning or correcting it, so responsibility for input correctness falls entirely on the human.
concepts.title: Truth Bias in LLM Completions

concepts.description: Checking whether entities in a ranked list or comparison are actually measured on comparable terms before accepting the ranking as meaningful.
concepts.title: Unfair Comparison Detection

concepts.description: Bounding how much a verification activity is worth spending on by computing the expected value of the information it would produce, before deciding whether to run it.
concepts.title: Value of Information for Verification Effort

concepts.description: Structuring verification reporting around subject status, evaluation methodology, and strategy adequacy to provide transparent audit trails.
concepts.title: Verification Accounting

concepts.description: Principles for designing concise, practical checklists that prevent critical errors during technical verification.
concepts.title: Verification Checklist Design

concepts.description: Placing a verification check as close as possible to the thing being verified, since each additional inferential hop between them is a separate opportunity to be wrong.
concepts.title: Verification Checkpoint Proximity

concepts.description: Standardized shorthand markers used during the verification process to track claim status, uncertainties, and revision decisions.
concepts.title: Verification Markup Conventions

concepts.description: The structural workflows organizing how claims are verified in a publishing or document lifecycle.

concepts.description: Heuristic consistency principles used by reviewers to identify contradictions, errors, and unstated assumptions in claims.
concepts.title: Verification Oracles

concepts.description: Automated detection tools and the fabrication techniques they target co-evolve, so no technological fix permanently solves verification — human judgment remains necessary regardless of tooling.
concepts.title: Verification Technology Arms Race

concepts.description: Treating an AI system's output as an unverified lead to check, not as a citable source, with transparent disclosure of where it was used.
concepts.title: Verifying Generative AI Outputs

concepts.description: The usually-unstated general principle that licenses an inference from a reason to a claim, distinct from both the reason and the evidence supporting it.
concepts.title: Warrants
